newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia corn higher due rupiah decline.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia corn higher due rupiah decline.

text.p: Indonesian corn prices were higher on Tuesday due mostly to the rupiah's decline against the U.S. dollar, traders said.
They also said players were closely monitoring the possible impact of the drought sweeping across most parts of the country on the corn harvest in East Java.
"Corn prices moved up because of the impact of the rupiah's decline against the U.S. dollar," one trader said. "The weaker rupiah has also forced some players to hold back imports."
"The volume involved is not substantial, but the importers would rather wait for the rupiah to stabilise against the dollar before taking fresh positions," he added.

The Indonesian currency had regained some strength against the dollar after plunging to a historic low one week ago but had shed some six percent against the U.S. currency when compared to levels before offshore speculative attacks forced the fall.
Another trader said corn prices were higher due also to the harvest in the key growing region of Lampung in South Sumatra coming to a close.
"There's not much corn coming from Lampung as the harvest is almost over and local supply will be tight," the trader said. "I think this helped to lift corn prices a little as well."

On the harvest in East Java, traders said crop arrival remained thin as the peak was only expected at the end of the year, but added that there was concern that output might be affected by the drought.
"I have been hearing that arrivals are low and that the size of the corn is also smaller than usual. I don't know if this is due to the drought, but there is some concern," he added.

Traders said corn imports continued to arrive in Indonesia, some ordered in anticipation of a poor harvest in East Java. One trader said about 150,000 tonnes of corn, mostly of Chinese origin, were expected to arrive by mid-August.
Traders said that August/September Chinese corn was being offered at $135-137 a tonne C&F, while U.S. corn was quoted at $132 for Panamax-sized shipments and $138-$139 for handy lots.
The local corn price was quoted at 400-410 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, up from 380-385 rupiah a week ago.
Traders said the soymeal market was quiet, with some 66,000 tonnes of soymeal expected to arrive by mid-August. One trader said South American soymeal was quoted at $279 C&F.
Local soymeal prices were stable at 895-900 rupiah.
